title: Change Record CR-001: Cell Voltage Maximum Limit Reduction 4200 mV -> 4150 mV (Cell Supplier Re-Specification)

It is not a test fixture: the change-lifecycle demonstration of the same subject (docs/artifacts/scenarios/change-lifecycles/change-001-voltage-threshold.json, FB2-SCN-CHG-000001) exists separately to exercise the corpus scenario gate, and the two are intentionally different artifacts with different jobs.

change_control.approval_note: No approval of any kind has been recorded. human_approval_status stays pending; decision.disposition below is a fictional workflow outcome, not a human sign-off.

trigger.source: Synthetic cell supplier change notification (fictional supplier, hypothetical project)
trigger.description: The cell supplier for the synthetic reference pack re-specifies the maximum charge voltage of the selected cell from 4200 mV to 4150 mV following a chemistry optimisation. Assumption FB2-ASM-001 states an operating range of 2.5 V-4.2 V and is invalidated by this notification; the supplier limit is mandatory and is not negotiable by the project.

impact_analysis.risk_assessment: The change is safety-improving in the hazard sense and availability-degrading in the noise sense, and those two effects pull in opposite directions. (1) Safety margin grows: FB2-ASM-002 places the thermal-runaway boundary above 4300 mV, so tripping at 4150 mV leaves 150 mV of boundary margin where the current 4200 mV limit leaves 100 mV. (2) Availability degrades: FB2-ASM-005 bounds measurement noise at sigma <= 5 mV, and FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 accepts a false-positive rate of 1E-6 events/hour for a 2-consecutive-sample debounce. At a 4200 mV limit the 3-sigma band (4215 mV) lies entirely above the limit, so a single noisy sample rarely crosses it; at 4150 mV the 3-sigma band (4165 mV) sits only 15 mV above the limit, so single-sample excursions below 4150 mV become materially more likely and a 2-of-2 rule starts tripping on noise. (3) The threshold ladder collapses: FB2-PRM-000001 currently carries warning=4150, derating=4180, shutdown=4200, so the new ceiling equals the existing warning level and the three-step ladder must be rebuilt rather than shifted. (4) The measurement-range statement in FB2-HW-TSR-000001 (2.5 V-4.2 V) narrows at the top end, and the plausibility stimulus in FB2-VER-TMS-000003 is specified against that range. (5) Assumptions FB2-ASM-001 and FB2-ASM-005 are invalidated and must be reissued, which in turn invalidates the noise basis of the accepted false-positive criterion. No residual risk is accepted: the debounce count is raised from 2 to 3 to restore the accepted false-positive rate at the new limit.

decision.decision_maker: change_control_board chair, fictional role identity 'A. Renner' (synthetic scenario character; not a foxBMS maintainer, not SoftwareDevLabs staff, not a real person)
decision.rationale: The supplier limit is mandatory, so the change cannot be rejected; there is no design freedom in the ceiling itself. The board therefore dispositions the request as approved in the fictional workflow sense and accepts the availability cost, because the safety margin increase (100 mV -> 150 mV to the FB2-ASM-002 runaway boundary) dominates a false-positive rate that is still bounded by the same 1E-6 events/hour criterion. Three dispositions are bundled and are each independently required: raise the debounce count from 2 to 3 to hold the false-positive rate; rebuild the warning/derating/shutdown ladder so that warning < derating < shutdown below the new ceiling; and reissue FB2-ASM-001 and FB2-ASM-005 rather than editing them in place, because their premises (cell operating range, noise sigma) are what changed.

synthetic_decision.label: synthetic_decision:change_control_board_chair:FB2-CHG-REF-000001
synthetic_decision.statement: decision.disposition 'approved' is a fictional workflow outcome of the synthetic-reference project's change control board. It is NOT a human approval, NOT a foxBMS maintainer decision, NOT a SoftwareDevLabs decision, and NOT a statement that any change was made to any real project. human_approval_status remains 'pending' and production_authorized remains false.

decision_disposition_scope: Approved means: the synthetic project proceeds to raise the revisions listed in new_revisions. It does not mean the revisions have been raised, that any test has been re-run, or that any baseline has been superseded. All of that is pending work at BAS-REF-002.

affected_artifact_rationale.current_text_binding: Statement names 'a debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms'; acceptance criterion 'Debounce filtering' accepts a false-positive rate of 1E-6 events/hour against Gaussian noise sigma=5 mV; acceptance criterion 'Limit accuracy' is 1 mV.
affected_artifact_rationale.why_re_review: This is the ASIL D requirement that the whole limit chain hangs off. It names the debounce count in prose and the noise model in its acceptance criteria, so both facts change.
affected_artifact_rationale.what_changes: Debounce count 2 -> 3; the accepted false-positive criterion is re-derived at the 4150 mV ceiling and restated against the reissued FB2-ASM-005; the 1 mV limit-accuracy criterion is re-checked against a 4150 mV comparison point (1 mV is 0.024% of the limit, so the criterion itself is unchanged, but its evidence must be regenerated at the new point).
affected_artifact_rationale.not_changed: The 5 ms classification latency and the 2 ms FAULT request latency are unaffected: lowering a comparison constant does not add work to the comparison path.

affected_artifact_rationale.current_text_binding: Hazardous event HE-01 (cell overvoltage during charging, ASIL D) is bounded by FB2-ASM-002 at above 4300 mV; degraded_states include 'Reduced charge current to 0.1C (derating)'.
affected_artifact_rationale.why_re_review: The hazard record states its degraded state in terms of the derating level, and the derating level is one of the three rungs of the ladder that this change rebuilds. The hazardous event itself does not move.
affected_artifact_rationale.what_changes: The degraded-state wording is re-expressed against the new derating level and the revised overvoltage margin (150 mV to the FB2-ASM-002 boundary instead of 100 mV) is recorded on the hazard record so the margin change is visible in the hazard analysis and not only in the parameter registry.
affected_artifact_rationale.not_changed: HE-01 severity/exposure/controllability (S3/E4/C3), its ASIL D allocation, and the safe-state list (contactors open, charging disabled until service) are untouched, because the safe state does not depend on the ceiling value.

affected_artifact_rationale.current_text_binding: Statement specifies +/-1.5 mV total accuracy 'over -40 C to +85 C for 2.5V-4.2V range'; acceptance criteria set total error 1.5 mV, LSB 0.5 mV, PEC single-bit detection 100%.
affected_artifact_rationale.why_re_review: The accuracy requirement is stated over a measurement range whose upper bound is the value being changed. Narrowing the top of the range is not a formality: the AFE must still be specified across 2500-4150 mV with the same total error, and the supplier's new limit removes the top 50 mV of the range the AFE was qualified over.
affected_artifact_rationale.what_changes: Range upper bound 4.2 V -> 4.15 V; the accuracy budget is re-allocated because the usable span shrinks by 50 mV while the same 1.5 mV total error (offset + gain + temperature drift) must hold, so the gain term's allowed share is unchanged but the calibration reference point moves from 4200 mV to 4150 mV; FB2-ASM-005 derives the 5 mV noise sigma from this +/-1.5 mV accuracy and is therefore reissued alongside it.
affected_artifact_rationale.not_changed: The 0.5 mV LSB and the 100% single-bit PEC detection coverage are unaffected by the ceiling value.

affected_artifact_rationale.current_text_binding: Constraint 'Debounce count configurable (default: 2)'; state machine DEBOUNCING -> VIOLATION_CONFIRMED guarded by 'consecutive_violations >= config'; action reset_debounce on the DEBOUNCING -> IDLE transition; timing constraint 'Check latency < 10 ms from database update'.
affected_artifact_rationale.why_re_review: The design is parameterised on the debounce count but hard-codes its default, and the guard is evaluated against the configured count. Changing the default without re-reviewing the design leaves the documented design and the intended behaviour disagreeing about the same number.
affected_artifact_rationale.what_changes: Default debounce count 2 -> 3; the 'reset_debounce' action on DEBOUNCING -> IDLE is retained unchanged, which matters because with a 3-sample debounce a partially-advanced counter that is not reset becomes materially more likely to produce a false fault - the defect recorded separately in FB2-MAN-CHG-000003 is what makes the reset action load-bearing here.
affected_artifact_rationale.not_changed: The state set, the transition guards other than the count, and the 10 ms check-latency constraint are unaffected. The limit comparison itself becomes a comparison against a configured value rather than a new code path, so no new transition is introduced.

affected_artifact_rationale.current_text_binding: Step 1: 'Inject cell voltage 4300 mV (above 4200 mV limit)'. Step 2: 'Repeat injection 2 times (debounce count)'. Step 3: 'Inject voltage 4100 mV (within limits)'. referenced_requirements: FB2-SAF-FSR-000002, FB2-SW-SWR-000002.
affected_artifact_rationale.why_re_review: The limit is embedded in the stimulus text and the debounce count is embedded in the step count, so the test as written no longer exercises the behaviour it was written to exercise. A test that still passes after this change would pass for the wrong reason, which is the specific failure mode a change record has to prevent.
affected_artifact_rationale.what_changes: Stimulus re-specified relative to a 4150 mV ceiling; step count raised to 3 to match the new debounce; a boundary case at 4150 mV is added because neither the old 4200 mV ceiling case nor a single 4300 mV excursion now probes the new comparison point; the in-limits step is re-based because 4100 mV is now only 50 mV below the limit and therefore no longer a comfortable in-limits point.
affected_artifact_rationale.not_changed: The test method (unit test on the SOA module with injected voltages) and its referenced requirements are unchanged.

suspect_link_rationale.why_suspect: The goal mitigates the hazard by making contactors open on a confirmed limit violation. The mechanism is unchanged, but the value at which it fires moves, so the goal's adequacy argument is re-argued at the new margin (150 mV instead of 100 mV to the FB2-ASM-002 boundary). Suspect means 'the reasoning must be re-shown', not 'the link is wrong'.
suspect_link_rationale.resolution: re-review at revision 1 of the goal; no link edit required if the re-argued margin still supports ASIL D.

suspect_link_rationale.why_suspect: The FSR's derivation from the goal rests on detecting an overvoltage within the hazard's operational situation. The FSR statement changes (debounce count), so the refinement must be re-derived rather than inherited.

The software requirement hard-codes both the 4.2 V ceiling and the 2-consecutive debounce in its own statement. The allocation is by statement, so once the FSR says 3, this link asserts an allocation to text that no longer says what the FSR says. The link's endpoints are both unchanged, which is exactly why it is easy to miss.
suspect_link_rationale.resolution: FB2-SW-SWR-000002 must be revised in the same change (see below) and the link re-affirmed at the new revisions.

suspect_link_rationale.why_suspect: The design's default debounce count is the number this change moves. An implements link whose design still says 2 while the requirement says 3 is a live claim that the design does not satisfy the requirement.
suspect_link_rationale.resolution: re-affirm at design revision 2 against the revised software requirement.

suspect_link_rationale.why_suspect: The only direct verifies link to the ASIL D limit-monitoring requirement, and the test stimulus names the old ceiling. The link currently asserts coverage that the stimulus no longer provides.
suspect_link_rationale.resolution: re-execute after the test revision; the link is re-affirmed only when the new stimulus exercises the 4150 mV comparison point.

suspect_link_rationale.why_suspect: Same test, second target. The software requirement duplicates the ceiling and debounce count in its own text, so the test must be re-checked against both targets, not one.
suspect_link_rationale.resolution: re-affirm together with FB2-LNK-SAF-000022 as a single re-execution.

suspect_link_rationale.why_suspect: The execution record is the evidence that the verifies links above rested on. If the measure changes, the result is no longer a result of the new measure; this is the link that carries the evidence invalidation.
suspect_link_rationale.resolution: supersede FB2-VER-EXE-000001 with a new execution at the post-change baseline. The stale record is retained, not rewritten.

suspect_link_registry_state: The baseline link registry (traceability/link-registry/synthetic_reference/links-cell-voltage.json) still records change_suspect_status=false on all seven links above. That is the correct state today: the change is approved only in the fictional workflow sense, no affected artifact has been revised, and no revision has been baselined. change_suspect_status becomes true for these links as part of establishing BAS-REF-002, at which point the registry flag and this record's suspect list must agree. This record deliberately does not pre-flip the baseline flags, because doing so would assert a change state that has not occurred.

parameter_registry_entries_affected.reason: The parameter that defines the cell voltage upper limit for SOA monitoring. It is the origin of this change, not a consequence of it.
The absolute tolerance band is expressed around the limit and must move with it.

parameter_registry_entries_affected.to: ladder to be re-derived below 4150 mV, retaining warning < derating < shutdown
parameter_registry_entries_affected.reason: The new ceiling equals the current warning level, so the three rungs cannot be shifted; they must be rebuilt. The corpus validator enforces the ordering for any parameter whose name contains 'max', so an unrevised ladder would be reported as a threshold-order violation.
Required to hold the 1E-6 events/hour false-positive rate that FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 accepts, given the 3-sigma noise band now sits 15 mV above the limit.

parameter_registry_entries_affected.to: re-review; 50 mV remains 1.2% of the ceiling
parameter_registry_entries_affected.reason: Hysteresis is proportional to the span, not to the ceiling, and 50 mV against a 4150 mV limit is wider than 50 mV was against 4200 mV. The ratio and the resulting cell-to-cell spread on recovery are re-checked rather than carried over silently.

parameter_registry_reference_note: FB2-PRM-000001 is an entry in the parameter registry (docs/artifacts/shared/parameter-registry.json and docs/artifacts/corpus/synthetic_reference/shared/parameter-registry.json), not a corpus artifact with a top-level id. It is therefore deliberately absent from impact_analysis.affected_artifacts and from required_updates: the change schema admits only ids matching ^FB2-[A-Z]{2,3}-[A-Z]{2,3}-[0-9]{6}$, and a link endpoint pointing at a registry entry rather than an artifact would dangle. The parameter change is recorded here instead, field by field, so the origin of the change is not lost.

assumptions_invalidated.current_statement: Lithium-ion cell chemistry with nominal voltage 3.7V, operating range 2.5V-4.2V
assumptions_invalidated.why: The supplier re-specifies the top of the range to 4.15 V. The assumption is invalidated, not edited, because its premise (the cell's own specification) is what changed.
assumptions_invalidated.action: reissue as a new assumption id at the post-change baseline; do not renumber the existing record

assumptions_invalidated.current_statement: Cell voltage measurement noise follows Gaussian distribution with sigma <= 5 mV
assumptions_invalidated.why: The noise sigma is derived from the AFE accuracy in FB2-HW-TSR-000001, whose qualified range narrows to 4.15 V. The false-positive analysis behind the 1E-6 events/hour criterion rests on this sigma, so it is reissued with the re-derived figure.
assumptions_invalidated.action: reissue and re-run the debounce false-positive analysis before the requirement's acceptance criterion is re-affirmed

assumptions_reconfirmed.statement: Thermal runaway initiates at cell voltage > 4.3V and temperature > 60 C
assumptions_reconfirmed.why_reconfirmed: Not invalidated by the supplier notification. It is reaffirmed here because the change moves the protection boundary closer to the runaway boundary and the arithmetic of that margin is the reason the request is dispositioned as approved.

evidence_invalidation.why: The evidence was produced against a measure whose stimulus names the 4200 mV ceiling. It remains a true record of what the old measure did, which is why it is superseded rather than edited. No evidence is deleted on a change.

evidence_reference_note: impact_analysis.affected_evidence is empty by schema, not by omission. The change schema admits only ids matching ^FB2-EVD-[A-Z]{2,4}-[0-9]{6}$, and no artifact with an FB2-EVD- prefix exists in either profile. The execution that this change really does invalidate is FB2-VER-EXE-000001, which does exist in synthetic_reference; it is named in evidence_invalidation above rather than forced into a slot whose id scheme does not admit it. The scenario fixture for the same change names FB2-VER-EXE-000001 in its affected_evidence because the scenario schema does not constrain that field.
reviews_note: impact_analysis.affected_reviews is empty by schema, not by omission. The change schema admits only ids matching ^FB2-REV-[A-Z]{2,4}-[0-9]{6}$, i.e. a review id with a two-to-four letter type segment. The corpus contains exactly one review artifact, FB2-REV-000001, which has no such segment, belongs to the as_is profile, and is an automated review of the reconstructed foxBMS artifacts rather than a review of the synthetic-reference change. There is therefore no review in the synthetic_reference profile for this change to invalidate. The review work this change requires is listed as re_review_scope below, and it cannot be discharged by this record.

re_review_scope.review_type_needed: safety_requirement_review with a separated challenge pass (ASIL D)
re_review_scope.why: The requirement is ASIL D and its accepted false-positive criterion is being re-derived, not merely re-worded.
The degraded-state boundary moves even though the hazardous event does not.
The accuracy budget is re-allocated over a narrower range; the review must confirm the calibration reference point moved rather than the tolerance being widened to compensate.
Default debounce count and the load-bearing role of the reset_debounce action.
Stimulus and step count are changed; the review must confirm the new stimulus probes the new comparison point rather than merely producing a pass.

reverification_criterion.selection_rule: Select every test measure whose stimulus, step count, or referenced requirement is changed by this change, plus every test measure that verifies a requirement on the path from the changed limit to the contactor reaction.

selected.basis: direct - stimulus and step count are rewritten in this change

regression - it exercises the contactor reaction on a confirmed violation; a false confirmation caused by the new limit would appear as a contactor test failure, so it is the cheapest detector of a threshold-side error
direct - its referenced requirement FB2-HW-TSR-000001 has its measurement range narrowed by this change

excluded.basis: no path from the cell voltage ceiling to the AFE communication integrity test; its referenced requirement FB2-HW-TSR-000002 is untouched by this change

reverification_criterion.acceptance_condition: Re-verification is complete when FB2-VER-TMS-000001 passes with a stimulus that exercises the 4150 mV comparison point, and when the re-run debounce analysis shows the 1E-6 events/hour false-positive rate holds at the new limit with a 3-sample debounce. A pass of the old stimulus does not satisfy this condition.

variant_impact.effect: The reference configuration is the configuration that changes; FB2-PRM-000001 carries configuration_selection [VAR-REF-001].

not_included_and_why.referenced_by: scenario fixtures FB2-SCN-CHG-000002 and FB2-SCN-CHG-000003, in impact_analysis.affected_artifacts and new_revisions[].artifact_id
not_included_and_why.status: resolves, but as the wrong kind of object: source anchors in docs/artifacts/sources/source-registry.json, not corpus artifacts
not_included_and_why.decision: not used in affected_artifacts or new_revisions; recorded instead as source_anchors_re_reviewed below
not_included_and_why.justification: These ids are real and they resolve - they are durable source anchors (AFE API header, SOA source file, LTC6811 slave schematic) and are the reason the fixtures can name code at all. But an anchor is not an artifact: it has no revision, no lifecycle_status, and no entry in the artifact index, so a 'changes' link pointed at one would dangle and the corpus validator would report a dangling link endpoint. Their id shape even matches the change schema's affected_artifacts pattern (FB2-SRC-COD-000001 fits ^FB2-[A-Z]{2,3}-[A-Z]{2,3}-[0-9]{6}$), which makes the mistake easy to make: a schema-valid id that still points at nothing of the required kind. The anchor-level consequence of this change is recorded in source_anchors_re_reviewed, where it belongs.

not_included_and_why.status: exists, but in the as_is profile only, and its id does not match the id scheme the change schema requires for this field

A synthetic-reference change record may not claim that an as_is review is invalidated by it: the two profiles are deliberately isolated, and a cross-profile reference here would be read as a claim about a real review of a real product.

differences_that_matter: The fixture validates structural completeness for the corpus scenario gate. This record is the change-management record of the synthetic project and is expected to be read by a reviewer, not by the gate.
The fixture keeps the pre-existing baseline link flags as it found them. This record explains the flag transition that the fixture leaves implicit.
The fixture names FB2-REV-000001 and FB2-VER-EXE-000001 in fields whose ids it does not have to resolve. This record resolves every id it names, and says so explicitly where a slot had to stay empty.
This record adds the parameter-registry field changes, the assumption invalidations, and the per-artifact and per-link re-review rationale that the fixture compresses into single strings.

implementation_note: No foxBMS source, test, configuration or build file is modified by this record, and none may be. The pinned foxBMS sources at commit 308028fb are untouched; the change described here exists only in the synthetic_reference profile. The synthetic project maps the SOA behaviour to src/app/application/soa/soa.c::SOA_CheckVoltageLimits, but that symbol does not exist in the pinned tree (verified by read-only search), so that mapping is a property of the fictional project and not a claim about the real repository.
